summary: Defines WebDAV, a set of methods, headers, and content types added to HTTP/1.1 for managing resource properties, creating and organizing collections, moving things around in the URL space, and locking to avoid edit collisions. It obsoletes RFC 2518 with minor revisions. It is a standards-track document.

plainLanguage.summary: WebDAV extends HTTP so clients can manage files and other web resources, not only retrieve them. It defines operations for properties, collections, copying, moving, and optional write locks.

questions: what is the difference between propfind and proppatch
subtitle: HTTP methods and rules for changing Web resources, organizing collections, managing properties, and coordinating edits.

tldr.problem: HTTP alone does not define a consistent way for clients to manage resource properties, collections, URL mappings, or concurrent edits.
tldr.mechanism: WebDAV adds authoring methods, XML request and response bodies, headers for depth and locking, and Multi-Status responses that report results for several resources or properties.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4918 replaces RFC 2518 with revisions based mainly on interoperability experience. It is a Proposed Standard updated by RFC 5689.

today: RFC 4918 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 2518 and is updated by RFC 5689. It revises the WebDAV HTTP extensions using interoperability experience.

sections.title: WebDAV Extends HTTP for Authoring
sections.content:
Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning (WebDAV) adds methods, headers, and content types to HTTP/1.1. These extensions let clients manage resource properties, create collections, change URL mappings, and use locks to coordinate edits.

This RFC updates RFC 2518 with revisions made mostly from interoperability experience. Versioning operations are not defined here; they are covered by a separate specification.
sections.plainLanguage: WebDAV adds standard HTTP operations for managing web resources. Clients can query details, create collections, copy or move resources, and coordinate some edits.

sections.title: Properties and Collections
sections.content:
A property is a name-value pair that describes a resource. A live property's syntax or value is checked or maintained by the server. A dead property is stored by the server as supplied, while the client is responsible for its meaning.

A collection is a resource that contains mappings from path segments to other resources. WebDAV methods can apply to just the collection, its immediate members, or its descendants. The client indicates this scope with a Depth value of 0, 1, or infinity.
sections.plainLanguage: Properties store information about a resource, and collections organize resources under a URL. A Depth value tells the server how far into a collection an operation should reach.

sections.title: Methods for Managing Resources
sections.content:
PROPFIND retrieves properties, and PROPPATCH sets or removes them. MKCOL creates a collection. COPY and MOVE use a Destination header to duplicate or relocate resources. LOCK and UNLOCK create and release write locks.

All DAV-compliant resources must support PROPFIND, PROPPATCH, COPY, and MOVE. PROPPATCH instructions are processed in document order and either all succeed or none do. The Overwrite header controls whether a copy or move may replace an existing destination.
sections.plainLanguage: WebDAV adds methods for reading and changing properties, making collections, copying and moving resources, and managing write locks. Each method has defined rules for its request and result.

sections.title: Write Locks and Their Limits
sections.content:
A write lock helps an authoring client avoid changes being overwritten while it edits a resource. A lock may be exclusive, which conflicts with any other lock on that resource, or shared, which allows several principals to hold locks at once.

Locking support is optional, and a lock can disappear at any time. A client must submit an authorized lock token when changing a locked resource. Locks reduce some edit conflicts but cannot stop a client that does not understand or use locking from overwriting content.
sections.plainLanguage: A write lock records who may change a resource and helps clients avoid overwriting one another. It only works when clients and servers use the lock rules, and the lock may disappear.

sections.title: Multi-Status Results
sections.content:
A request that affects several resources or properties may return 207 Multi-Status. Its XML body gives each resource's URL and its result; PROPFIND and PROPPATCH can also report results for individual properties.

The overall 207 code does not say whether the whole operation succeeded. The client must inspect the body. WebDAV also defines status codes including 422 Unprocessable Entity, 423 Locked, 424 Failed Dependency, and 507 Insufficient Storage.
sections.plainLanguage: A 207 response contains a report for multiple resources or properties. The client reads that report to determine which actions succeeded and which failed.

sections.title: Discovering Resource Capabilities
sections.content:
A resource advertises its WebDAV compliance classes in the DAV header of an OPTIONS response. Class 1 identifies support for the base requirements. Class 2 adds locking support and related properties and headers.

Class 3 advertises support for the revisions in RFC 4918 and also requires class 1. Compliance applies to resources, not necessarily to every resource on a server.
sections.plainLanguage: The DAV header tells a client which feature class a resource supports. Class 2 includes locks, while class 3 identifies support for the revisions in this RFC.

sections.title: Authentication, Privacy, and XML Risks
sections.content:
Because WebDAV permits changes, authentication protects resource integrity as well as access. Basic authentication must not be used over an insecure connection, and WebDAV applications must support Digest authentication.

The RFC also warns about denial of service from large uploads, recursive operations, or many requests; private details in properties or lock-owner information; and risks from XML external or deeply nested entities. Servers that allow content publishing may also need precautions against malicious content.
sections.plainLanguage: Changing remote resources requires authentication and careful handling of XML requests. Servers also need to protect private properties and control operations that consume excessive resources.

items.desc: Retrieves properties at a chosen depth.

items.label: Create a collection
items.desc: Creates a collection at the request URL.

items.label: Copy a resource
items.desc: Copies to the URI in the Destination header.

items.label: Create or refresh a lock
items.desc: Obtains or refreshes a write lock.

items.label: Release a lock
items.desc: Removes the lock identified by its token.
